questions.text:
Given below are two statements :
Statement I : The function $f:\mathbf{R}\to\mathbf{R}$ defined by $f(x)=\dfrac{x}{1+|x|}$ is one-one.
Statement II : The function $f:\mathbf{R}\to\mathbf{R}$ defined by $f(x)=\dfrac{x^2+4x-30}{x^2-8x+18}$ is many-one.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.sol:
Statement I: for $x\ge0$, $f(x)=\dfrac{x}{1+x}$ and for $x<0$, $f(x)=\dfrac{x}{1-x}$; both pieces are strictly increasing and $f$ keeps the sign of $x$, so $f$ is one-one. True.
Statement II: the denominator has discriminant $64-72<0$, so $f$ is defined on all of $\mathbf{R}$. $f(x)=c$ gives $(1-c)x^2+(4+8c)x-(30+18c)=0$, which has two distinct real roots for suitable $c$ (e.g. $c=0$: $x^2+4x-30=0$). So $f$ is many-one. True.

questions.text: Let $\mathrm{A}=\{z\in\mathbb{C}:|z-2|\le4\}$ and $\mathrm{B}=\{z\in\mathbb{C}:|z-2|+|z+2|=5\}$. Then the max $\{|z_1-z_2|:z_1\in\mathrm{A}$ and $z_2\in\mathrm{B}\}$ is :
questions.sol:
A is the disc with centre $2$ and radius 4. B is the ellipse with foci $\pm2$ and $2a=5$: $\dfrac{x^2}{25/4}+\dfrac{y^2}{9/4}=1$.
The maximum is $4+$ (greatest distance from $(2,0)$ to the ellipse). On the ellipse, distance$^2=(x-2)^2+\dfrac94\left(1-\dfrac{4x^2}{25}\right)=\dfrac{16}{25}x^2-4x+\dfrac{25}{4}$, largest at $x=-\dfrac52$: $\dfrac{81}{4}$, i.e. $\dfrac92$.
Maximum $=4+\dfrac92=\dfrac{17}{2}$.

questions.text: Let the arithmetic mean of $\dfrac1a$ and $\dfrac1b$ be $\dfrac{5}{16}$, $a>2$. If $\alpha$ is such that $a, 4, \alpha, b$ are in A.P., then the equation $\alpha x^2-ax+2(\alpha-2b)=0$ has :
options: complex roots of magnitude less than 2
one root in $(1, 4)$ and another in $(-2, 0)$
one root in $(0, 2)$ and another in $(-4, -2)$
questions.sol:
With common difference $d=4-a$: $\alpha=8-a$ and $b=12-2a$.
$\dfrac1a+\dfrac1b=\dfrac58$ gives $8(12-a)=5a(12-2a)$, i.e. $5a^2-34a+48=0$, so $a=\dfrac{24}{5}$ (as $a>2$). Then $\alpha=\dfrac{16}{5}$, $b=\dfrac{12}{5}$.
The equation becomes $16x^2-24x-16=0$, i.e. $2x^2-3x-2=0$, with roots $2$ and $-\dfrac12$: one in $(1,4)$ and one in $(-2,0)$.

questions.text: The sum of the coefficients of $x^{499}$ and $x^{500}$ in $(1+x)^{1000}+x(1+x)^{999}+x^2(1+x)^{998}+\ldots+x^{1000}$ is :
questions.sol:
Coefficient of $x^r$ in $\displaystyle\sum_{k=0}^{1000}x^k(1+x)^{1000-k}$ is $\displaystyle\sum_{k=0}^{r}\binom{1000-k}{1000-r}=\sum_{n=1000-r}^{1000}\binom{n}{1000-r}=\binom{1001}{1001-r}=\binom{1001}{r}$.
Required sum $=\binom{1001}{499}+\binom{1001}{500}=\binom{1002}{500}$.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements :
Statement I : $25^{13}+20^{13}+8^{13}+3^{13}$ is divisible by 7.
Statement II : The integral part of $\left(7+4\sqrt3\right)^{25}$ is an odd number.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.sol:
Statement I: for odd $n$, $a^n+b^n$ is divisible by $a+b$. $25^{13}+3^{13}$ is divisible by 28 and $20^{13}+8^{13}$ by 28, so the sum is divisible by 7. True.
Statement II: let $(7+4\sqrt3)^{25}=I+f$ with $0\le f<1$ and $f'=(7-4\sqrt3)^{25}\in(0,1)$. Then $I+f+f'$ is an even integer (the irrational terms cancel and the rest doubles), and $0<f+f'<2$ forces $f+f'=1$. So $I$ is odd. True.

questions.text:
The probability distribution of a random variable X is given below :
X$4k$$\dfrac{30}{7}k$$\dfrac{32}{7}k$$\dfrac{34}{7}k$$\dfrac{36}{7}k$$\dfrac{38}{7}k$$\dfrac{40}{7}k$$6k$
P(X)$\dfrac{2}{15}$$\dfrac{1}{15}$$\dfrac{2}{15}$$\dfrac15$$\dfrac{1}{15}$$\dfrac{2}{15}$$\dfrac15$$\dfrac{1}{15}$
If $\mathrm E(\mathrm X)=\dfrac{263}{15}$, then $\mathrm P(\mathrm X<20)$ is equal to :
questions.sol:
$15\,\mathrm E(\mathrm X)=k\left[8+\dfrac{30+64+102+36+76+120}{7}+6\right]=k\left(14+\dfrac{428}{7}\right)=\dfrac{526}{7}k$.
$\dfrac{526k}{7}=263$ gives $k=\dfrac72$, so the values are 14, 15, 16, 17, 18, 19, 20, 21.
$\mathrm P(\mathrm X<20)=1-\dfrac15-\dfrac1{15}=\dfrac{11}{15}$.

questions.text: Let the circle $x^2+y^2=4$ intersect $x$-axis at the points $\mathrm A(a, 0)$, $a>0$ and $\mathrm B(b, 0)$. Let $\mathrm P(2\cos\alpha, 2\sin\alpha)$, $0<\alpha<\dfrac\pi2$ and $\mathrm Q(2\cos\beta, 2\sin\beta)$ be two points such that $(\alpha-\beta)=\dfrac\pi2$. Then the point of intersection of AQ and BP lies on :
questions.sol:
A $=(2,0)$, B $=(-2,0)$. The lines AQ and BP meet at a point R outside the circle, and the angle between two secants is half the difference of the intercepted arcs: arc BQ $=90^\circ+\alpha$ and arc AP $=\alpha$, so $\angle$ARB $=\tfrac12(90^\circ)=45^\circ$.
So R lies on a circle through A and B on which AB subtends $45^\circ$: its centre is on the y-axis with $\angle$AOB at the centre $=90^\circ$, i.e. centre $(0,2)$ and radius $2\sqrt2$: $x^2+(y-2)^2=8$, i.e. $x^2+y^2-4y-4=0$.
Check with $\alpha=\pi/4$: R $=(2\sqrt2,2)$ satisfies it.

questions.text: Let the ellipse $\mathrm{E}:\dfrac{x^2}{144}+\dfrac{y^2}{169}=1$ and the hyperbola $\mathrm{H}:\dfrac{x^2}{16}-\dfrac{y^2}{\lambda^2}=-1$ have the same foci. If e and L respectively denote the eccentricity and the length of the latus rectum of H, then the value of $24(\mathrm e+\mathrm L)$ is :
questions.sol:
E has foci $(0,\pm5)$ since $169-144=25$.
H is $\dfrac{y^2}{\lambda^2}-\dfrac{x^2}{16}=1$ with foci $(0,\pm\sqrt{\lambda^2+16})$, so $\lambda^2=9$.
$e=\dfrac53$ and $L=\dfrac{2\cdot16}{3}=\dfrac{32}{3}$, so $24(e+L)=24\cdot\dfrac{37}{3}=296$.

questions.text: Let P be a point in the plane of the vectors $\overrightarrow{\mathrm{AB}}=3\hat i+\hat j-\hat k$ and $\overrightarrow{\mathrm{AC}}=\hat i-\hat j+3\hat k$ such that P is equidistant from the lines AB and AC. If $\left|\overrightarrow{\mathrm{AP}}\right|=\dfrac{\sqrt5}{2}$, then the area of the triangle ABP is :
questions.sol:
$|\overrightarrow{\mathrm{AB}}|=|\overrightarrow{\mathrm{AC}}|=\sqrt{11}$, so the bisector of angle BAC is along $\overrightarrow{\mathrm{AB}}+\overrightarrow{\mathrm{AC}}=(4,0,2)$, of length $2\sqrt5$.
$\overrightarrow{\mathrm{AP}}=\dfrac{\sqrt5}{2}\cdot\dfrac{(4,0,2)}{2\sqrt5}=\left(1,0,\tfrac12\right)$.
$\overrightarrow{\mathrm{AB}}\times\overrightarrow{\mathrm{AP}}=\left(\tfrac12,-\tfrac52,-1\right)$, of length $\sqrt{7.5}=\dfrac{\sqrt{30}}{2}$; area $=\dfrac{\sqrt{30}}{4}$.

questions.text: Let $\mathrm{Q}(a, b, c)$ be the image of the point $\mathrm{P}(3, 2, 1)$ in the line $\dfrac{x-1}{1}=\dfrac y2=\dfrac{z-1}{1}$. Then the distance of Q from the line $\dfrac{x-9}{3}=\dfrac{y-9}{2}=\dfrac{z-5}{-2}$ is
questions.sol:
Foot of the perpendicular: $(1+t,2t,1+t)$ with $(t-2)+2(2t-2)+t=0$, so $t=1$ and the foot is $(2,2,2)$. Hence Q $=(1,2,3)$.
The second line passes through $(9,9,5)$ with direction $(3,2,-2)$. The vector to Q is $(-8,-7,-2)$, and its cross product with $(3,2,-2)$ is $(18,-22,5)$ of length $\sqrt{833}=7\sqrt{17}$.
Distance $=\dfrac{7\sqrt{17}}{\sqrt{17}}=7$.

questions.text:
Let $f(x)=\displaystyle\lim_{\theta\to0}\left(\dfrac{\cos\pi x-x^{\left(\frac2\theta\right)}\sin(x-1)}{1+x^{\left(\frac2\theta\right)}(x-1)}\right)$, $x\in\mathbf{R}$. Consider the following two statements :
(I) $f(x)$ is discontinous at $x=1$.
(II) $f(x)$ is continous at $x=-1$.
Then,
questions.sol:
Write $n=2/\theta\to\infty$ (an even power in the intended reading). For $|x|<1$, $x^n\to0$ and $f(x)=\cos\pi x$. For $|x|>1$, $f(x)=-\dfrac{\sin(x-1)}{x-1}$.
At $x=1$: $f(1)=-1$, left limit $\cos\pi=-1$, right limit $-1$. Continuous, so (I) is false.
At $x=-1$: right limit $\cos(-\pi)=-1$, left limit $-\dfrac{\sin(-2)}{-2}=-\dfrac{\sin2}{2}\ne-1$. Discontinuous, so (II) is false.

questions.text: Let $[\cdot]$ denote the greatest integer function. Then $\displaystyle\int_{-\pi/2}^{\pi/2}\left(\dfrac{12(3+[x])}{3+[\sin x]+[\cos x]}\right)dx$ is equal to :
questions.sol:
Except at isolated points, $[\cos x]=0$; $[\sin x]=-1$ for $x<0$ and $0$ for $x>0$. So the denominator is 2 on $(-\pi/2,0)$ and 3 on $(0,\pi/2)$.
$(-\pi/2,-1)$: $[x]=-2$, integrand 6. $(-1,0)$: $[x]=-1$, integrand 12. $(0,1)$: integrand 12. $(1,\pi/2)$: $[x]=1$, integrand 16.
Integral $=6\left(\tfrac\pi2-1\right)+12+12+16\left(\tfrac\pi2-1\right)=11\pi+2$.

questions.text: Let $f(x)=\displaystyle\int\dfrac{dx}{x^{\left(\frac23\right)}+2x^{\left(\frac12\right)}}$ be such that $f(0)=-26+24\log_e(2)$. If $f(1)=a+b\log_e(3)$, where $a, b\in\mathbf{Z}$, then $a+b$ is equal to :
questions.sol:
Put $x=t^6$: $\displaystyle\int\dfrac{6t^5\,dt}{t^4+2t^3}=\int\dfrac{6t^2}{t+2}dt=\int6\left(t-2+\dfrac{4}{t+2}\right)dt=3t^2-12t+24\ln(t+2)+C$.
$f(0)=24\ln2+C=-26+24\ln2$ gives $C=-26$.
$f(1)=3-12+24\ln3-26=-35+24\ln3$, so $a+b=-11$.

questions.text: Let $y=y(x)$ be the solution of the differential equation $x\dfrac{dy}{dx}-y=x^2\cot x$, $x\in(0,\pi)$. If $y\left(\dfrac\pi2\right)=\dfrac\pi2$, then $6y\left(\dfrac\pi6\right)-8y\left(\dfrac\pi4\right)$ is equal to :
questions.sol:
Dividing by $x^2$: $\dfrac{d}{dx}\left(\dfrac yx\right)=\cot x$, so $\dfrac yx=\ln\sin x+C$. $y(\pi/2)=\pi/2$ gives $C=1$, so $y=x(1+\ln\sin x)$.
$6y(\pi/6)=\pi(1-\ln2)$ and $8y(\pi/4)=2\pi\left(1-\tfrac12\ln2\right)=2\pi-\pi\ln2$.
Difference $=-\pi$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: Let $\mathrm{P_1}:y=4x^2$ and $\mathrm{P_2}:y=x^2+27$ be two parabolas. If the area of the bounded region enclosed between $\mathrm{P_1}$ and $\mathrm{P_2}$ is six times the area of the bounded region enclosed between the line $y=\alpha x$, $\alpha>0$ and $\mathrm{P_1}$, then $\alpha$ is equal to :
questions.sol:
$\mathrm{P_1}$ and $\mathrm{P_2}$ meet at $x=\pm3$: area $=\displaystyle\int_{-3}^{3}(27-3x^2)\,dx=108$.
Line and $\mathrm{P_1}$ meet at $x=0$ and $x=\alpha/4$: area $=\displaystyle\int_0^{\alpha/4}(\alpha x-4x^2)\,dx=\dfrac{\alpha^3}{96}$.
$108=\dfrac{6\alpha^3}{96}$ gives $\alpha^3=1728$, $\alpha=12$.

questions.text: Let $\mathrm A=\begin{bmatrix}3&-4\\1&-1\end{bmatrix}$ and B be two matrices such that $\mathrm A^{100}=100\mathrm B+\mathrm I$. Then the sum of all the elements of $\mathrm B^{100}$ is _________
questions.sol:
$\mathrm A=\mathrm I+\mathrm N$ with $\mathrm N=\begin{bmatrix}2&-4\\1&-2\end{bmatrix}$ and $\mathrm N^2=\mathrm O$.
So $\mathrm A^{100}=\mathrm I+100\mathrm N$, giving $\mathrm B=\mathrm N$ and $\mathrm B^{100}=\mathrm O$.
Sum of elements $=0$.

questions.text: If $\displaystyle\sum_{r=1}^{25}\left(\dfrac{r}{r^4+r^2+1}\right)=\dfrac pq$, where p and q are positive integers such that $\gcd(p, q)=1$, then $p+q$ is equal to __________.
questions.sol:
$r^4+r^2+1=(r^2-r+1)(r^2+r+1)$, so $\dfrac{r}{r^4+r^2+1}=\dfrac12\left(\dfrac{1}{r^2-r+1}-\dfrac{1}{r^2+r+1}\right)$, which telescopes.
Sum $=\dfrac12\left(1-\dfrac1{651}\right)=\dfrac{325}{651}$ (coprime, since $651=3\cdot7\cdot31$ and $325=5^2\cdot13$).
$p+q=976$.

questions.text: Three persons enter in a lift at the ground floor. The lift will go upto $10^{\text{th}}$ floor. The number of ways, in which the three persons can exit the lift at three different floors, if the lift does not stop at first, second and third floors, is equal to __________.
questions.sol:
The available floors are the 4th to the 10th, i.e. 7 floors.
Three persons at three different floors: $7\times6\times5=210$.

questions.text: If the distance of the point $\mathrm P(43, \alpha, \beta)$, $\beta<0$, from the line $\vec r=4\hat i-\hat k+\mu\left(2\hat i+3\hat k\right)$, $\mu\in\mathbf{R}$ along a line with direction ratios $3, -1, 0$ is $13\sqrt{10}$, then $\alpha^2+\beta^2$ is equal to ________
questions.sol:
A point at distance $|s|\sqrt{10}$ from P along $(3,-1,0)$ is $(43+3s,\ \alpha-s,\ \beta)$. On the line, $y=0$, so $s=\alpha$ and $|\alpha|=13$.
Also $43+3\alpha=4+2\mu$ and $\beta=-1+3\mu$. $\alpha=13$ gives $\mu=39$, $\beta=116$ (rejected); $\alpha=-13$ gives $\mu=0$, $\beta=-1$.
$\alpha^2+\beta^2=169+1=170$.

questions.text: Let $f$ be a differentiable function satisfying $f(x)=1-2x+\displaystyle\int_0^x e^{(x-t)}f(t)\,dt$, $x\in\mathbf{R}$ and let $g(x)=\displaystyle\int_0^x(f(t)+2)^{15}(t-4)^6(t+12)^{17}\,dt$, $x\in\mathbf{R}$. If p and q are respectively the points of local minima and local maxima of g, then the value of $|p+q|$ is equal to _________.
questions.sol:
Multiply by $e^{-x}$ and differentiate: $f'=2f+2x-3$ with $f(0)=1$. Trying $f=Ax+B$: $A=-1$, $B=1$, and this satisfies $f(0)=1$, so $f(x)=1-x$.
$g'(x)=(3-x)^{15}(x-4)^6(x+12)^{17}$. The sign changes from $-$ to $+$ at $x=-12$ (local minimum) and from $+$ to $-$ at $x=3$ (local maximum); $x=4$ is not an extremum (even power).
$|p+q|=|-12+3|=9$.

questions.text: The time period of a simple harmonic oscillator is $T=2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac km}$. Measured value of mass $(m)$ of the object is 10 g with an accuracy of 10 mg and time for 50 oscillations of the spring is found to be 60 s using a watch of 2 s resolution. Percentage error in determination of spring constant $(k)$ is__________%.
questions.sol:
Whichever way the relation is written, $k$ is proportional to $m^{\pm1}T^{\pm2}$, so $\dfrac{\Delta k}{k}=\dfrac{\Delta m}{m}+2\dfrac{\Delta T}{T}$.
$\dfrac{\Delta m}{m}=\dfrac{10\ \mathrm{mg}}{10\ \mathrm g}=0.1\%$ and $\dfrac{\Delta T}{T}=\dfrac{2}{60}=3.33\%$.
Total $\approx0.1+6.67\approx6.76\%$.

questions.text: As shown in the figure, a spring is kept in a stretched position with some extension by holding the masses 1 kg and 0.2 kg with a separation more than spring natural length and are released. Assuming the horizontal surface to be frictionless, the angular frequency (in SI unit) of the system is :
questions.sol:
Reduced mass $\mu=\dfrac{1\times0.2}{1.2}=\dfrac16$ kg.
$\omega=\sqrt{\dfrac k\mu}=\sqrt{150\times6}=30$ rad/s.

questions.text: A small block of mass $m$ slides down from the top of a frictionless inclined surface, while the inclined plane is moving towards left with constant acceleration $a_0$. The angle between the inclined plane and ground is $\theta$ and its base length is $L$. Assuming that initially the small block is at the top of the inclined plane, the time it takes to reach the lowest point of the inclined plane is _________.
questions.sol:
In the frame of the incline a pseudo force $ma_0$ acts to the right, i.e. with a component $a_0\cos\theta$ up the slope (the block slides down towards the left).
Acceleration along the incline: $g\sin\theta-a_0\cos\theta$; distance $\dfrac{L}{\cos\theta}$.
$t=\sqrt{\dfrac{2L}{\cos\theta(g\sin\theta-a_0\cos\theta)}}=\sqrt{\dfrac{4L}{g\sin2\theta-a_0(1+\cos2\theta)}}$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
A particle starts moving from time $t=0$ and its coordinate is given as $x(t)=4t^3-3t$
A. The particle returns to its original position (origin) 0.866 units later
B. The particle is 1 unit away from origin at its turning point
C. Acceleration of the particle is non-negative
D. The particle is 0.5 units away from origin at its turning point
E. Particle never turns back as acceleration is non-negative
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.sol:
$x=0$ again at $4t^2=3$, $t=\dfrac{\sqrt3}{2}\approx0.866$: A true.
$v=12t^2-3=0$ at $t=0.5$, where $x=0.5-1.5=-1$: 1 unit from the origin, so B true and D false; the particle does turn back, so E false.
$a=24t\ge0$ for $t\ge0$: C true. Answer: A, B, C.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: When the position vector $\vec r=x\hat i+y\hat j+z\hat k$ changes sign as $-\vec r$, which one of the following vector will not flip under sign change ?
questions.sol:
Velocity, linear momentum and acceleration are derived directly from $\vec r$ and change sign with it.
Angular momentum $\vec L=\vec r\times\vec p$ is a product of two vectors that both change sign, so it does not flip.

questions.text: The speed of a longitudinal wave in a metallic bar is 400 m/s. If the density and Young's modulus of the bar material are increased by 0.5% and 1%, respectively then the speed of the wave is changed approximately to __________ m/s.
questions.sol:
$v=\sqrt{Y/\rho}$, so $\dfrac{\Delta v}{v}=\dfrac12\left(\dfrac{\Delta Y}{Y}-\dfrac{\Delta\rho}{\rho}\right)=\dfrac12(1-0.5)\%=0.25\%$.
New speed $\approx400\times1.0025=401$ m/s.

questions.text: The mean free path of a molecule of diameter $5\times10^{-10}$ m at the temperature $41\ ^\circ$C and pressure $1.38\times10^5$ Pa, is given as ________ m. (Given $k_B=1.38\times10^{-23}$ J/K).
questions.sol:
$\lambda=\dfrac{k_BT}{\sqrt2\,\pi d^2p}$ with $T=314$ K.
$\lambda=\dfrac{1.38\times10^{-23}\times314}{\sqrt2\times3.14\times25\times10^{-20}\times1.38\times10^5}=\dfrac{100\times10^{-23}}{\sqrt2\times25\times10^{-15}}=\dfrac{4\times10^{-8}}{\sqrt2}=2\sqrt2\times10^{-8}$ m.

questions.text:
Identify the correct statements :
A. Electrostatic field lines form closed loops .
B. The electric field lines point radially outward when charge is greater than zero.
C. The Gauss - Law is valid only for inverse - square force.
D. The workdone in moving a charged particle in a static electric field around a closed path is zero.
E. The motion of a particle under Coulomb's force must take place in a plane.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.sol:
A is false: electrostatic field lines start on positive and end on negative charges and never form closed loops.
B is true for a positive point charge. C is true: Gauss's law follows from the $1/r^2$ dependence. D is true: the electrostatic field is conservative.
E is true: the Coulomb force from a fixed charge is central, so angular momentum is conserved and the motion stays in one plane.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
Identify the correct statements :
A. Effective capacitance of a series combination of capacitors is always smaller than the smallest capacitance of the capacitor in the combination.
B. When a dielectric medium is placed between the charged plates of a capacitor, displacement of charges cannot occur due to insulation property of dielectric.
C. Increasing of area of capacitor plate or decreasing of thickness of dielectric is an alternate method to increase the capacitance.
D. For a point charge, concentric spherical shells centered at the location of the charge are equipotential surfaces.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.sol:
A: $\dfrac1C=\sum\dfrac1{C_i}>\dfrac1{C_{\min}}$, so true.
B: a dielectric is polarised, i.e. its bound charges are displaced, so false.
C: $C=\dfrac{\varepsilon A}{d}$, so true. D: the potential of a point charge depends only on $r$, so true. Answer: A, C and D.

questions.text: A Wheatstone bridge is initially at room temperature and all arms of the bridge have same value of resistances $(R_1=R_2=R_3=R_4)$. When $R_3$ resistance is heated to some temperature, its resistance value has gone up by 10%. The potential difference $(V_a-V_b)$ (after $R_3$ is heated) is __________V.
questions.sol:
Each side of the bridge is a divider across 40 V, with the positive terminal at the top junction. Taking the bottom junction as zero:
$V_a=40\cdot\dfrac{R}{2R}=20$ V and $V_b=40\cdot\dfrac{R}{1.1R+R}=\dfrac{40}{2.1}=19.05$ V.
$V_a-V_b\approx0.95$ V.

questions.text:
A long cylindrical conductor with large cross section carries an electric current distributed uniformly over its cross-section. Magnetic field due to this current is :
A. maximum at either ends of the conductor and minimum at the midpoint
B. maximum at the axis of the conductor
C. minimum at the surface of the conductor
D. minimum at the axis of the conductor
E. same at all points in the cross-section of the conductor
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.note: The official final key gives (2), D only. Read across a cross-section, statement A (largest at the ends of a diameter, least at its midpoint on the axis) would also be true, which would make (1) correct; the key is followed for marking.
questions.sol:
Ampere's law inside a uniformly carrying cylinder gives $B=\dfrac{\mu_0Ir}{2\pi R^2}$: zero on the axis and largest at the surface ($r=R$).
So D is true, and B, C and E are false.
A speaks of the 'ends' and 'midpoint' of the conductor; along a long straight conductor the field does not change from the ends to the middle, so A is not accepted. The final key gives D only.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: Which one of the following is not a measurable quantity ?
questions.sol:
Only differences of potential can be measured: a voltmeter always reads the potential of one point relative to another. The potential (voltage) of a single point depends on the arbitrary choice of zero, so it is not measurable by itself.
Potential difference, resistance and displacement current ($\varepsilon_0\,d\Phi_E/dt$, inferred from the changing field) are measurable.

questions.text: A plane electromagnetic wave is moving in free space with velocity $c=3\times10^8$ m/s and its electric field is given as $\vec E=54\sin(kz-\omega t)\,\hat j$ V/m, where $\hat j$ is the unit vector along $y$-axis. The magnetic field vector $\vec B$ of the wave is :
questions.sol:
$B_0=\dfrac{E_0}{c}=\dfrac{54}{3\times10^8}=1.8\times10^{-7}$ T.
The disturbance travels along $+z$ and $\vec E\times\vec B$ must point along $+z$: $\hat j\times(-\hat i)=\hat k$, so $\vec B$ is along $-\hat i$.
$\vec B=-1.8\times10^{-7}\sin(kz-\omega t)\,\hat i$ T.

questions.text: For a transparent prism, if the angle of minimum deviation is equal to its refracting angle, the refractive index $n$ of the prism satisfies.
questions.sol:
With $\delta_m=A$: $n=\dfrac{\sin A}{\sin(A/2)}=2\cos\dfrac A2$.
At minimum deviation the angle of incidence is $\dfrac{A+\delta_m}{2}=A$, which cannot exceed $90^\circ$, so $0<\dfrac A2\le45^\circ$.
Hence $\sqrt2\le n<2$, i.e. option (4).

questions.text: A biconvex lens is formed by using two thin planoconvex lenses, as shown in the figure. The refractive index and radius of curved surfaces are also mentioned in figure. When an object is placed on the left side of lens at a distance of 30 cm from the biconvex lens, the magnification of the image will be :
questions.sol:
Powers add: $\dfrac1f=\dfrac{1.5-1}{15}+\dfrac{1.2-1}{12}=\dfrac1{30}+\dfrac1{60}=\dfrac1{20}$, so $f=20$ cm.
$\dfrac1v=\dfrac1{20}-\dfrac1{30}=\dfrac1{60}$, $v=60$ cm.
$m=\dfrac vu=\dfrac{60}{-30}=-2$.

questions.text: Number of photons of equal energy emitted per second by a 6 mW laser source operating at 663 nm is __________. (Given : $h=6.63\times10^{-34}$ J.s and $c=3\times10^8$ m/s)
questions.sol:
Photon energy $E=\dfrac{hc}{\lambda}=\dfrac{6.63\times10^{-34}\times3\times10^8}{663\times10^{-9}}=3\times10^{-19}$ J.
$N=\dfrac{P}{E}=\dfrac{6\times10^{-3}}{3\times10^{-19}}=2\times10^{16}$ per second.

questions.text: Two p-n junction diodes $D_1$ and $D_2$ are connected as shown in figure. $A$ and $B$ are input signals and $C$ is the output. The given circuit will function as a __________.
questions.sol:
The anodes of both diodes are joined to C, which is pulled up to 5 V through R; the cathodes go to A and B.
If either input is low (0), that diode conducts and holds C low. Only when both inputs are high are both diodes off, and C is high. This is an AND gate.

questions.text: A fly wheel having mass 3 kg and radius 5 m is free to rotate about a horizontal axis. A string having negligible mass is wound around the wheel and the loose end of the string is connected to 3 kg mass. The mass is kept at rest initially and released. Kinetic energy of the wheel when the mass descends by 3 m is _________ J. $(g=10\ \mathrm{m/s^2})$
questions.sol:
Treat the wheel as a uniform disc: $I=\tfrac12MR^2=37.5$ kg m$^2$, and $v=\omega R$.
Energy: $3\times10\times3=90=\tfrac12(3)v^2+\tfrac12(37.5)\dfrac{v^2}{25}=2.25v^2$, so $v^2=40$.
Kinetic energy of the wheel $=\tfrac12I\omega^2=0.75\times40=30$ J.

questions.text: Two tuning forks $A$ and $B$ are sounded together giving rise to 8 beats in 2 s. When fork $A$ is loaded with wax, the beat frequency is reduced to 4 beats in 2 s. If the original frequency of tuning fork $B$ is 380 Hz then original frequency of tuning fork $A$ is _________ Hz.
questions.sol:
Beat frequency 4 Hz, so $f_A=384$ or $376$ Hz. Loading A with wax lowers $f_A$.
The beat frequency falls to 2 Hz, which happens only if $f_A$ was above 380 Hz: $f_A=384$ Hz.

questions.text: An inductor stores 16 J of magnetic field energy and dissipates 32 W of thermal energy due to its resistance when an a.c. current of 2 A (rms) and frequency 50 Hz flows through it. The ratio of inductive reactance to its resistance is __________. $(\pi=3.14)$
questions.sol:
Resistance: $I_{\text{rms}}^2R=32$ gives $R=8\ \Omega$.
Energy: $\tfrac12LI^2=16$ with $I=2$ A gives $L=8$ H.
$X_L=2\pi fL=2(3.14)(50)(8)=2512\ \Omega$, so $\dfrac{X_L}{R}=314$.

questions.text: A thermodynamic system is taken through the cyclic process $ABC$ as shown in the figure. The total work done by the system during the cycle $ABC$ is ________ J.
questions.sol:
The cycle A(2 m$^3$, 100 Pa) to B(5 m$^3$, 300 Pa) to C(5 m$^3$, 100 Pa) and back to A runs clockwise on the P-V diagram, so the work done by the system is positive.
Work $=$ area of the triangle $=\tfrac12\times3\times200=300$ J.

questions.text: A beam of light consisting of wavelengths 650 nm and 550 nm illuminates the Young's double slits with separation of 2 mm such that the interference fringes are formed on a screen, placed at a distance of 1.2 m from the slits. The least distance of a point from the central maximum, where the bright fringes due to both the wavelengths coincide, is ________ $\times10^{-5}$ m.
questions.sol:
Bright fringes coincide when $n_1(650)=n_2(550)$, i.e. $13n_1=11n_2$; the smallest choice is $n_1=11$.
$y=\dfrac{11\times650\times10^{-9}\times1.2}{2\times10^{-3}}=4.29\times10^{-3}$ m $=429\times10^{-5}$ m.

questions.text:
For the given reaction;
$\mathrm{CaCO_3+2HCl\longrightarrow CaCl_2+H_2O+CO_2}$
If 90 g $\mathrm{CaCO_3}$ is added to 300 mL of HCl which contains 38.55% HCl by mass and has density 1.13 g mL$^{-1}$, then which of the following option is correct ?
Given molar mass of H, Cl, Ca and O are 1, 35.5, 40 and 16 g mol$^{-1}$ respectively.
questions.sol:
Mass of HCl $=300\times1.13\times0.3855=130.68$ g. $\mathrm{CaCO_3}=0.9$ mol needs $1.8$ mol $=65.7$ g HCl, so $\mathrm{CaCO_3}$ is the limiting reagent.
HCl left $=130.68-65.7\approx64.97$ g.

questions.text: The wavelength of photon 'A' is 400 nm. The frequency of photon 'B' is $10^{16}\ \mathrm s^{-1}$. The wave number of photon 'C' is $10^4\ \mathrm{cm^{-1}}$. The correct order of energy of these photons is :
questions.sol:
Compare frequencies: A: $ u=\dfrac{3 imes10^8}{400 imes10^{-9}}=7.5 imes10^{14}$ Hz. B: $10^{16}$ Hz. C: $\lambda=10^{-4}$ cm $=1000$ nm, so $ u=3 imes10^{14}$ Hz.
$E=h u$, so B $>$ A $>$ C.

questions.text: The plot of $\log_{10}K$ vs $\dfrac1T$ gives a straight line. The intercept and slope respectively are (where K is equilibrium constant).
questions.sol:
$\Delta G^\circ=-2.303RT\log K=\Delta H^\circ-T\Delta S^\circ$, so $\log K=\dfrac{\Delta S^\circ}{2.303R}-\dfrac{\Delta H^\circ}{2.303R}\cdot\dfrac1T$.
Intercept $\dfrac{\Delta S^\circ}{2.303R}$ and slope $-\dfrac{\Delta H^\circ}{2.303R}$.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements :
Statement I : The increasing order of boiling point of hydrogen halides is HCl < HBr < HI < HF.
Statement II : The increasing order of melting point of hydrogen halides is HCl < HBr < HF < HI.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.sol:
Boiling points (K): HCl 189, HBr 206, HI 238, HF 293 (hydrogen bonding), so Statement I is true.
Melting points (K): HCl 159, HBr 187, HF 190, HI 222, so Statement II is also true.

questions.text:
Consider the following statements about manganate and permanganate ions. Identify the correct statements.
A. The geometry of both manganate and permanganate ions is tetrahedral.
B. The oxidation states of Mn in manganate and permanganate are +7 and +6, respectively.
C. Oxidation of Mn(II) salt by peroxodisulphate gives manganate ion as the final product.
D. Manganate ion is paramagnetic and permanganate ions is diamagnetic.
E. Acidified permanganate ion reduces oxalate, nitrite and iodide ions.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.sol:
A: both $\mathrm{MnO_4^{2-}}$ and $\mathrm{MnO_4^-}$ are tetrahedral (true). B: the states are $+6$ (manganate) and $+7$ (permanganate), the reverse of the statement (false).
C: peroxodisulphate oxidises $\mathrm{Mn^{2+}}$ to permanganate (false). D: manganate is $d^1$ (paramagnetic) and permanganate $d^0$ (diamagnetic) (true).
E: acidified permanganate oxidises oxalate, nitrite and iodide; it does not reduce them (false). Answer: A and D only.

questions.text:
Identify the correct statements :
The presence of $-\mathrm{NO_2}$ group in benzene ring
A. activates the ring towards electrophilic substitutions.
B. deactivates the ring towards electrophilic substitutions.
C. activates the ring towards nucleophilic substitutions.
D. deactivates the ring towards nucleophilic substitutions.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.sol: The nitro group withdraws electron density from the ring ($-R$ and $-I$). This makes attack by electrophiles harder (B) and stabilises the negatively charged intermediate formed in nucleophilic substitution, e.g. of o- and p-nitrochlorobenzene (C).

questions.text:
A student performed analysis of aliphatic organic compound 'X' which on analysis gave C = 61.01%, H = 15.25%, N = 23.74%.
This compound, on treatment with $\mathrm{HNO_2/H_2O}$ produced another compound 'Y' which did not contain any nitrogen atom. However, the compound 'Y' upon controlled oxidation produced another compound 'Z' that responded to iodoform test.
The structure of 'X' is :
questions.sol:
C : H : N $=\dfrac{61.01}{12}:\dfrac{15.25}{1}:\dfrac{23.74}{14}=5.08:15.25:1.70=3:9:1$, so X is $\mathrm{C_3H_9N}$ (aliphatic), which rules out (3) ($\mathrm{C_4}$) and (2) (aromatic).
Nitrous acid converts a primary amine to an alcohol Y. Oxidation of Y must give a methyl ketone for the iodoform test: propan-2-ol gives acetone. So X is propan-2-amine, $\mathrm{(CH_3)_2CHNH_2}$ (propan-1-amine would give propanal).

For strong electrolyte $\Lambda_m$ increases slowly with dilution and can be represented by the equation
$\Lambda_m=\Lambda^\circ_m-Ac^{1/2}$
Molar conductivity values of the solutions of strong electrolyte AB at 18$^\circ$C are given below :
c [mol L$^{-1}$]0.040.090.160.25
$\Lambda_m$ [S cm$^2$ mol$^{-1}$]96.195.795.394.9
The value of constant A based on the above data [in S cm$^2$ mol$^{-1}$/(mol/L)$^{1/2}$] unit is __________.

questions.text:
A volume of $x$ mL of 5 M $\mathrm{NaHCO_3}$ solution was mixed with 10 mL of 2 M $\mathrm{H_2CO_3}$ solution to make an electrolytic buffer. If the same buffer was used in the following electrochemical cell to record a cell potential of 235.3 mV, then the value of $x$ = __________ mL (nearest integer).
$\mathrm{Sn(s)\,|\,Sn(OH)_6^{2-}\,(0.5\ M)\,|\,HSnO_2^-\,(0.05\ M)\,|\,OH^-\,|\,Bi_2O_3(s)\,|\,Bi(s)}$
Consider upto one place of decimal for intermediate calculations
Given : $\mathrm{E^\circ_{HSnO_2^-|Sn(OH)_6^{2-}}=-0.9\ V}$
$\mathrm{E^\circ_{Bi_2O_3|Bi}=-0.44\ V}$
$\mathrm{pKa_{(H_2CO_3)}}=6.11$
$\dfrac{2.303\,RT}{F}=0.059$ V
Antilog (1.29) = 19.5
questions.sol:
Anode: $\mathrm{HSnO_2^-+3OH^-+H_2O\to Sn(OH)_6^{2-}+2e^-}$; cathode: $\mathrm{Bi_2O_3+3H_2O+6e^-\to2Bi+6OH^-}$. $E^\circ_{\text{cell}}=-0.44-(-0.9)=0.46$ V.
$E=0.46-\dfrac{0.059}{2}\log\dfrac{[\mathrm{Sn(OH)_6^{2-}}]}{[\mathrm{HSnO_2^-}][\mathrm{OH^-}]}=0.46-0.0295\log\dfrac{10}{[\mathrm{OH^-}]}=0.2353$.
$\log\dfrac{10}{[\mathrm{OH^-}]}=7.6$, so pOH $=6.6$ and pH $=7.4$.
Buffer: $7.4=6.11+\log\dfrac{5x}{20}$, so $\dfrac{5x}{20}=$ antilog $1.29=19.5$ and $x=78$ mL.

questions.text:
$\mathrm{A\longrightarrow B}$ (first reaction)
$\mathrm{C\longrightarrow D}$ (second reaction)
Consider the above two first-order reactions. The rate constant for first reaction at 500 K is double of the same at 300 K. At 500 K, 50% of the reaction becomes complete in 2 hour. The activation energy of the second reaction is half of that of first reaction. If the rate constant at 500 K of the second reaction becomes double of the rate constant of first reaction at the same temperature; then rate constant for the second reaction at 300 K is __________ $\times10^{-1}$ hour$^{-1}$ (nearest integer).
questions.sol:
First reaction at 500 K: $k_1=\dfrac{\ln2}{2}=0.3466$ h$^{-1}$; second: $k_2(500)=0.693$ h$^{-1}$.
For the first reaction $\ln\dfrac{k(500)}{k(300)}=\dfrac{E_a}{R}\left(\dfrac1{300}-\dfrac1{500}\right)=\ln2$. With half the activation energy, the second reaction's ratio is $e^{(\ln2)/2}=\sqrt2$.
$k_2(300)=\dfrac{0.693}{\sqrt2}=0.49$ h$^{-1}\approx5\times10^{-1}$ h$^{-1}$.

questions.text: The number of isoelectronic species among $\mathrm{Sc^{3+}}$, $\mathrm{Cr^{2+}}$, $\mathrm{Mn^{3+}}$, $\mathrm{Co^{3+}}$ and $\mathrm{Fe^{3+}}$ is 'n'. If 'n' moles of AgCl is formed during the reaction of complex with formula $\mathrm{CoCl_3(en)_2NH_3}$ with excess of $\mathrm{AgNO_3}$ solution, then the number of electrons present in the $t_{2g}$ orbital of the complex is __________.
questions.sol:
Electrons: $\mathrm{Sc^{3+}}$ 18, $\mathrm{Cr^{2+}}$ 22, $\mathrm{Mn^{3+}}$ 22, $\mathrm{Co^{3+}}$ 24, $\mathrm{Fe^{3+}}$ 23. Only $\mathrm{Cr^{2+}}$ and $\mathrm{Mn^{3+}}$ are isoelectronic, so $n=2$.
Two ionisable chlorides means the complex is $\mathrm{[Co(en)_2(NH_3)Cl]Cl_2}$, with $\mathrm{Co^{3+}}$ ($d^6$) and strong-field ligands: $t_{2g}^6e_g^0$.
Electrons in $t_{2g}$: 6.
